newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ MAKE SWIFT PROGRESS AGAINST SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ MAKE SWIFT PROGRESS AGAINST SRI LANKA.

text.p: New Zealand had wrested back some of the initiative by lunch on the second day of the second test against Sri Lanka on Saturday.
Responding to New Zealand's first innings total of 222 on Friday, Sri Lanka were in some bother at 75 for three at the lunch break.

Two wickets in the space of three balls to remove Hashan Tillerkaratne and dangerman Aravinda de Silva greatly assisted the home team's cause after the Sri Lankans had looked composed to reach 57 for one.

Seam bowler Simon Doull expected extra bounce from the pitch to see Tillerkaratne glove an easy catch to second slip, while de Silva, who made just three and nought in the first test, failed again when left arm spinner Daniel Vettori found an inside edge, which struck de Silva's pad before ballooning in the air.
Fast bowler Heath Davis had earlier accounted for opener Sanath Jayasuriya for 20 when he induced an edge into the slips cordon.
Jayasuriya's opening partner Roshan Mahanama held the Sri Lankans together, looking composed at at ease while making an unbeaten 41 in two hours.
He will resume after the interval with captain Arjuna Ranatunga, who was on four.
Davis had one for 22, Doull one for 17 and Vettori one for 13 from seven tidy overs for New Zealand.
